rows.grounds: nominative subject, the person observing the fast
purpose compound indicating the aim of preserving vital breath or life
optative expressing that one must not fall or come to ruin
ablative indicating fasting as the cause to be avoided when life is at risk

items.question: Should preservation of life override the observance of prescribed fasting?
premises: A person must act for the protection of life.
Fasting must not cause a person to perish.
items.inference: The duty to preserve life limits the observance of fasting when fasting becomes life-threatening.
uncertainties: bhraśyet may mean fall away, decline, or perish; rendered here as perish in the context of life protection.
items.plain_english: A person should not perish from fasting, for the sake of preserving life.
